explanation: The theorem is about the library's own Chevalley-group definitions: rootSpan, pinnedX, rootOperatorFamily and ringCommContained_pos. It says that a closed subset J of positive roots gives a subgroup that is normal in the span of S. Mathlib has no Chevalley groups, root-subgroup spans or commutator relations of this kind. The proof only uses generic subgroup lemmas such as Subgroup.normal_subgroupOf_iff_le_normalizer, iSup₂_le and Subgroup.closure_le. These are the tools of the argument, not statements of the result. I did not run searches over the Mathlib sources, so this answer rests on my knowledge of Mathlib and not on a grep.
